A novel

Arthur Vale Is Dead

Milk. Light bulbs. Call Sarah.

Arthur Vale spent thirty-one years settling insurance claims. He always assumed that when he went, people would have kind things to say about him. They do, mostly. They just aren't saying them to him.

Complete trilogy

The
Hydrarchy.

The oceans have been gone for three hundred years. What water is left is metered, taxed and sold back by the cup.

Book one

Once Was Ocean

Everyone in the Rust-Gutter knows the story of a boy, a boat and a light across a sea that no longer exists. Nobody believes it. Then Calder learns the sea did not vanish. It was hidden.

UK → US →

Book two

Rising Deep

Calder gave the world back its sea. Now it will not stop rising: a hand's width a month, quietly, in the night, and every road leads to the last dry country.

UK → US →

Book three

The Absolute Deep

There is no shore left. There is only the Count. Four thousand people on a fleet of small hulls, and a system built to keep them alive that begins deciding who is worth keeping.

About

J Banners.

Most of J Banners' books start with something nobody asked for, and then keep going long after a sensible person would have stopped.

He reads across literary fiction, crime, science fiction, dark fantasy and noir. Away from the page he makes music, usually late and usually with the door shut, and cooks with more ambition than a weeknight strictly requires.

The Register

One letter a month.

The real document behind a book, and one line about the next release. Nothing else, and never more than once a month.
